title: Human vs humanoid robot cage fight goes viral
key_facts: In mid-September a company called Robot Entertainment Kombat (REK) hosted what it said was the first human-on-robot cage fight in California, per Futurism.
Futurism says the robot was controlled by a human handler behind the scenes and the human fighter acted out the robot's strikes in a wrestling style.
The California State Athletic Commission has apparently sent a cease-and-desist order to anyone holding, promoting or sponsoring unsanctioned human-versus-humanoid-robot cage fights.
Per the letter REK's founder Cix Liv posted, the organisers must stop at once or face a misdemeanor charge.
Futurism says the commission seems to object to the missing permits, not to robot fights as such; California law requires its approval before a full-contact martial arts event.

Yahoo Sports adds that the fight was on 18 Sep 2026 between content creator Frankie LaPenna and an EngineAI T800 robot, that the letter is dated 23 Sep and attributed to executive officer Andy Foster, and that a human operator drove the robot through a VR headset.
Yahoo Sports says the outcome of the fight is disputed and that REK's founder posted the notice online, writing 'We made it, boys'.
quote_evidence: behind the scenes, the robot was controlled by a human handler
In its letter, the Athletic Commission didn't appear to take issue with the human-robot bouts per se, but with the organizers' failure to secure the required permits.
California's athletic commission sent a cease-and-desist to a fight promotion for staging an unsanctioned human-versus-humanoid-robot bout, and the promoter celebrated by posting the notice online.
why_it_matters_hint: Existing combat-sport permit rules are being applied to a new kind of robot entertainment, and the letter is known mainly through the promoter's own post.
event_date: Fight mid-Sep 2026 (18 Sep per Yahoo Sports); cease-and-desist letter dated 23 Sep 2026 per Yahoo Sports.
notes: Original item was CyberGuy (cyberguy.com), which returned HTTP 403, so the story was written from Futurism, cross-checked with Yahoo Sports. Futurism says 'apparently'; the letter is seen only through the promoter's post. Yahoo Sports details (date, names, VR headset) come from one outlet and are not independently confirmed. Underlying events are before 2 Oct 2026.
